title: File chips on a waiting message, round 2: on the same line

steps.path: The waiting strip just above the message box
steps.headline: The file chips now sit on the same line, right after the words.
steps.changed: You asked for the chips in line after the text. They now follow the words on one line instead of sitting on a second row. Icon and file name, up to three, then "+N more".
steps.notice: The waiting strip keeps its old height.
steps.risk: Practice data; not yet tried with a real waiting message.

steps.path: The waiting strip, with a long message
steps.headline: With a long message, the words are cut short so the chips stay visible.
steps.changed: On a computer the strip never wraps. A long message ends in "..." before the chips.
steps.notice: You always see which files are attached, even when the message is long.
steps.risk: You see less of a long waiting message than before when files are attached. Edit still shows all of it.

steps.path: The waiting strip at phone width
steps.headline: On a phone, the chips drop under the words when they do not fit beside them.
steps.changed: At phone width, words and chips share the line only if both fit. Otherwise the chips go underneath, so the words are not squeezed to nothing.
steps.notice: On a narrow phone with two chips, the strip is two rows.
steps.risk: This differs from the computer, where it is always one line.
